metadata.purpose: Build a lightweight, fast, keyboard-first application launcher inspired by the most commonly used launcher workflows, while intentionally avoiding a Chromium/Electron runtime and keeping idle memory usage low.

rules.rule: Every task must always have a status attribute.
Before starting a task, change its status from pending to in_progress.
Mark a task done only after its acceptance criteria have been verified.
If a task cannot continue, set status to blocked and add a blocker note explaining exactly why.
When task status changes, update the task's updated_at attribute using ISO-8601 local or UTC time.
Do not silently delete tasks. If a task becomes unnecessary, mark it skipped and explain why in notes.
Keep this XML file as the source of truth for implementation progress.

codex_role.instruction: You are the implementation agent for this repository. Work iteratively, keep the project buildable after each meaningful step, and update this XML file as progress is made.

Prefer native Windows APIs and lightweight Rust dependencies. Do not introduce Electron, WebView2, Node.js, Tauri, a browser runtime, or another heavyweight embedded runtime unless the user explicitly changes the requirements.
Optimize for perceived latency, low idle RAM, low background CPU, simple architecture, and easy maintenance.
Avoid premature complexity. The first milestone is a reliable launcher prototype, not a full Raycast clone.
When choosing third-party crates, use maintained crates compatible with the current stable Rust toolchain. Pin versions in Cargo.lock and document why each non-trivial dependency exists.

product_requirements.requirement: A global hotkey must show or hide the launcher. Default prototype hotkey: Alt+Space.
The launcher must provide a focused search input immediately after opening.
The launcher must index installed/start-menu applications without scanning the entire disk on every invocation.
Typing an application name must produce ranked fuzzy-search results and Enter must launch the selected application.
The application must support an internal command system so commands such as help and help install can be typed into the launcher.
The command "help" must open an in-app Help view or Help panel.
The command "help install" must show the full installation/setup guide inside the application without requiring an internet connection.

The installation guide shown by help install must be sourced from a repository documentation file and embedded into the binary at compile time, so the repository guide and in-app guide cannot silently drift apart.
Escape must close or hide the launcher without terminating the background process.
Up/Down keys must change the selected result; Enter must execute the selected result.
Recent launches should influence ranking, but this may be implemented after the basic prototype works.

performance.target: Idle working set target: under 40 MB on a normal Windows 11 x64 development machine.
Stretch idle working set target: under 30 MB.
Background CPU while idle: approximately 0% under normal conditions.
Hotkey-to-visible-window target after warm startup: under 50 ms where practical.
Cold process startup target: under 250 ms for the prototype, with a preferred target under 150 ms.
Do not perform a full filesystem crawl on each launcher invocation.

quality.target: The project must compile with the current stable Rust toolchain on Windows.
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings should pass before the prototype is considered complete.
Core search/ranking logic must have unit tests.
Unexpected failures must be logged without crashing the background launcher when recovery is possible.

architecture.design_goal: Keep the launcher resident in memory with a small native window hidden most of the time. The hotkey should toggle visibility, while the search index remains small and readily available.

recommended_modules.module: Process lifecycle, startup, shutdown, event loop, and dependency wiring.
Win32-specific hotkey registration, shell integration, window placement, process launch, and Windows paths.
Native/lightweight launcher window, input handling, result list, help view, and keyboard navigation.
Discovers application shortcuts and executable launch targets from known Windows locations.
Query normalization, fuzzy matching, scoring, tie-breaking, and result ranking.
Internal command registry and command execution, including help and help install.
Optional lightweight persistence for recent launches and usage frequency.
Compile-time embedded help/install documentation and rendering adapters.
Local-only diagnostics/logging. No remote telemetry in the prototype.

data_flow.step: Process starts and registers the global hotkey.
Application index is loaded from cache or rebuilt from known application locations.
Launcher window becomes visible and search input receives focus.
User input is parsed as either an internal command or a normal application query.
Results are ranked from the in-memory index.
Enter executes the selected command or launches the selected application.
Launcher hides again and returns to idle state.

repository_layout.path: Canonical installation guide embedded by help install.
Project overview, quick start, architecture summary, and development commands.

implementation_rules.rule: Prefer the official windows crate or equivalent maintained Win32 bindings for native Windows API access.
For the first prototype, use a lightweight native Rust UI approach. Prefer direct Win32 controls/drawing or another small native solution. Do not use a browser-rendered UI.
Keep main.rs small; move logic into modules that can be tested independently.
Do not block the UI thread with application discovery or slow I/O.
Cache application discovery results and rebuild only when needed.
Application discovery should focus on known sources such as the user and system Start Menu Programs directories and other documented shell locations. Do not recursively scan all fixed drives.
Normalize search text case-insensitively and handle Unicode safely.
Prefer bounded data structures and avoid retaining unnecessary icons/images in memory.
If icons are used, load them lazily or use a small bounded cache.
The prototype must not send analytics, queries, installed app names, or clipboard contents to a remote service.

command.name: help
command.behavior: Open the in-app Help view. Display available internal commands, keyboard shortcuts, basic usage, troubleshooting links within the local help system, and a clearly visible instruction that "help install" opens the installation guide.

command.name: help install
command.behavior: Render the contents of docs/INSTALL.md inside the application. This must work offline.
command.implementation_requirement: Embed docs/INSTALL.md during compilation, for example with Rust include_str! or a similarly simple compile-time mechanism.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The command works on a machine with no internet access.
The text shown in-app matches the committed docs/INSTALL.md content from the build.
The user can scroll through the guide using keyboard and/or mouse.
Escape returns to the normal launcher or closes the Help view predictably.

installation_guide_required_content.instruction: Create docs/INSTALL.md with enough detail that a developer can set up, build, run, test, and optionally package the prototype from a clean Windows machine.

section.title: System Requirements
section.item: Windows 10 or Windows 11 x64.
Administrator access may be needed for installing developer tools, but LiteCast itself should not require elevation for normal use.
Git.
Current stable Rust toolchain via rustup.
MSVC C++ build tools required by the x86_64-pc-windows-msvc target.

section.title: Install Development Tools
section.item: Install Git.
Install rustup and select the stable toolchain.
Install Visual Studio Build Tools with the Desktop development with C++ workload or the minimum MSVC/Windows SDK components needed by Rust MSVC.
Verify rustc --version, cargo --version, and git --version.

section.title: Run in Development
section.item: Press Alt+Space to open the launcher.
Type an installed application name.
Press Enter to launch it.
Type help to open Help.
Type help install to display this installation guide inside LiteCast.

section.title: Release Build
section.item: Document where the resulting executable is located.
Document how to run the release executable directly.

section.title: Optional Local Installation
section.item: Provide a script or documented command to copy the release binary into a per-user application directory.
Optionally create a Start Menu shortcut.
Optionally configure startup-at-login, but keep this opt-in.

section.title: Troubleshooting
section.item: Rust/MSVC linker errors.
Global hotkey conflict.
No applications found after initial indexing.
Application shortcut cannot be launched.
Window appears off-screen after monitor topology changes.
How to run reindex.
How to view local logs.

section.title: Uninstall Development Build
section.item: Exit LiteCast using the quit command or tray/menu equivalent if implemented.
Remove any startup entry created by optional install steps.
Delete the installed executable/config directory if the user wants a complete removal.

task.title: Initialize Rust project

actions.action: Create a new Rust binary project named litecast.
Use Rust edition supported by the current stable toolchain.
Configure the Windows MSVC x64 target.
Commit Cargo.lock.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: cargo build succeeds on Windows x64.
The executable starts and exits cleanly.

task.notes: Initialized Rust binary project 'litecast' with edition 2024 targeting x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. cargo build and cargo run succeed.

task.title: Create repository structure

actions.action: Create the modules and docs directories described in repository_layout.
Keep main.rs minimal.
Add a .gitignore appropriate for Rust and Windows development.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Project structure matches the documented architecture.
cargo build still succeeds.

task.notes: Created repository structure with all modules (app, platform_windows, ui, indexer, search, commands, docs, history, telemetry_local) and .gitignore. Cargo build, fmt, and clippy pass.

task.title: Create canonical installation documentation

actions.action: Create docs/INSTALL.md using installation_guide_required_content from this prompt.
Create docs/HELP.md for general usage and command documentation.
Create README.md with quick start and architecture summary.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A new developer can follow docs/INSTALL.md from a clean Windows machine without undocumented prerequisites.
README.md points to docs/INSTALL.md.

task.notes: Created docs/INSTALL.md, docs/HELP.md, and README.md with all required sections and references.

task.title: Create Windows application lifecycle

actions.action: Implement a long-running Windows process with a native event/message loop.
Ensure the process can stay idle without polling continuously.
Add clean shutdown handling.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Idle CPU usage is effectively zero in Task Manager under normal conditions.
The process exits cleanly using the internal quit path or normal shutdown.

task.notes: Implemented native Win32 message loop with GetMessageW blocking on idle (0% CPU) and clean quit handler.

task.title: Register Alt+Space global hotkey

actions.action: Register Alt+Space with the Windows global hotkey API.
Handle registration failure gracefully.
Log a clear error if another application already owns the hotkey.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Alt+Space is received while LiteCast is in the background.
A hotkey conflict does not crash the process.

task.notes: Registered Alt+Space global hotkey with RegisterHotKey, graceful logging on conflict without crashing.

task.title: Create show/hide launcher window behavior

actions.action: Create a small native launcher window.
Center it on the active monitor or use a sensible remembered position.
Show it when Alt+Space is pressed.
Hide it on Escape.
Focus the query input immediately when shown.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Alt+Space consistently opens the launcher.
Escape hides it without ending the process.
The user can type immediately without clicking.

task.notes: Native popup window created, centered dynamically on active monitor, shown on Alt+Space, hidden on Escape, input focused immediately.

task.title: Discover installed applications from known Windows locations

actions.action: Enumerate user Start Menu Programs.
Enumerate system Start Menu Programs.
Resolve .lnk shortcuts using an appropriate Windows shell API or maintained implementation.
Capture display name, launch target, optional arguments, source path, and a stable identifier.
Do not recursively scan entire drives.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Common installed desktop applications appear in the generated index.
Broken shortcuts are ignored or reported without crashing.

task.notes: Implemented Start Menu scanning across user and system Programs directories. Discovered 153 applications on development machine.

task.title: Add index cache

actions.action: Persist a compact per-user cache in an appropriate local application data directory.
Load the cache on startup.
Rebuild when the cache is missing, invalid, or explicitly refreshed.
Use a small and maintainable serialization format.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Second startup does not require full shortcut rediscovery unless needed.
Corrupt cache data is handled by rebuilding safely.

task.notes: Implemented JSON cache serialization at %LOCALAPPDATA%/LiteCast/cache.json with graceful fallback rebuilding.

task.title: Add reindex command backend

actions.action: Expose index rebuild as a callable operation used later by the internal command registry.
Ensure reindex does not freeze the launcher UI.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A full reindex can be triggered at runtime.
The UI remains responsive during the rebuild.

task.notes: Exposed AppIndex::rebuild() and connected to reindex command.

task.title: Implement query normalization

actions.action: Trim whitespace.
Perform case-insensitive matching.
Handle Unicode input without panics.
Prepare normalized strings for ranking without unnecessary allocations on every keystroke.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Equivalent case variants return equivalent results.
Unicode application names can be searched.

task.notes: Implemented normalize_query with Unicode lowercase folding, verified in test_normalization.

task.title: Implement fuzzy ranking

actions.action: Rank exact matches highest.
Rank prefix matches above loose fuzzy matches.
Support subsequence/fuzzy matching for partial names.
Use deterministic tie-breaking.
Return only a bounded number of visible results.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Searching "code" ranks Visual Studio Code near the top when installed.
Exact application name matches rank first.
Ranking unit tests cover exact, prefix, fuzzy, and no-match cases.

task.notes: Implemented exact, prefix, word-prefix, and subsequence fuzzy ranking with deterministic tie-breaking. Covered by tests.

task.title: Render search results

actions.action: Display a bounded result list under the query input.
Highlight the current selection.
Support Up and Down navigation.
Reset selection predictably when query changes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Typing updates results interactively.
Keyboard navigation never selects an invalid index.

task.notes: Rendered double-buffered GDI result list with dynamic window resizing, selected item highlight, Up/Down navigation.

task.title: Launch selected application

actions.action: Launch the resolved shortcut/target using the appropriate Windows shell execution mechanism.
Hide the launcher after successful execution.
Display or log a helpful failure message when execution fails.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Enter launches the selected application.
Launching an invalid target does not crash LiteCast.

task.notes: Implemented ShellExecuteW execution on Enter, launcher hides automatically upon execution, errors logged without crash.

task.title: Create internal command registry

actions.action: Define a command abstraction with name, aliases, description, usage, and execute behavior.
Detect internal commands before treating input as an application query.
Keep command matching deterministic and testable.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Commands can be registered without modifying the search engine.
Unknown commands fail gracefully or fall back to normal search according to a documented rule.

task.notes: Implemented parse_command for help, help install, reindex, quit. Verified in test_parse_known_commands.

task.title: Embed help documentation into the binary

actions.action: Embed docs/HELP.md at compile time.
Embed docs/INSTALL.md at compile time.
Expose both through src/docs.rs.
Ensure missing files fail the build rather than creating an empty help experience.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The compiled application can display both documents with the network disabled.
Editing docs/INSTALL.md and rebuilding changes help install output.

task.notes: Embedded docs/HELP.md and docs/INSTALL.md via include_str! in src/docs.rs for offline availability.

task.title: Implement help command

actions.action: Register the command help.
Open a scrollable Help view using embedded docs/HELP.md.
List commands and keyboard shortcuts.
Include an obvious reference to help install.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Typing help and pressing Enter opens Help.
The user can navigate/scroll the Help view.
Escape returns to the normal launcher state.

task.notes: Implemented in-app scrollable Help view rendered via GDI with Up/Down and PageUp/PageDown navigation, Esc returns to search.

task.title: Implement help install command

actions.action: Register the command help install.
Render embedded docs/INSTALL.md inside the Help view.
Preserve readable headings, code blocks, commands, and lists even if the UI uses a simplified Markdown renderer.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Typing help install and pressing Enter opens the complete installation guide.
The command works offline.
The content is derived from docs/INSTALL.md in the build.

task.notes: Implemented help install rendering complete embedded docs/INSTALL.md guide offline inside launcher window.

task.title: Implement reindex and quit commands

actions.action: Register reindex and connect it to the index rebuild operation.
Register quit and perform a clean process shutdown.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: reindex rebuilds application data without restarting LiteCast.
quit exits the background process cleanly.

task.notes: Implemented reindex (in-memory index update + cache save) and quit (clean window destruction and event loop exit).

task.title: Persist recent launches

actions.action: Store only the minimal stable application identifier, launch count, and recent timestamp data needed for ranking.
Keep the file compact and local-only.
Bound growth or prune old entries.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: History survives application restart.
History storage remains small and bounded.

task.notes: Implemented UsageHistory persistence at %LOCALAPPDATA%/LiteCast/history.json.

task.title: Blend usage history into ranking

actions.action: Give a modest score boost to frequently/recently launched applications.
Do not allow usage history to overwhelm strong textual matches.
Add deterministic ranking tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Frequently used apps move upward for ambiguous queries.
An exact textual match remains dominant.

task.notes: Blended history boost with bounded cap (max +50) in search_apps_with_history. Verified by test_usage_history_boost.

task.title: Add local diagnostic logging

actions.action: Log startup failures, hotkey conflicts, index failures, launch failures, and cache recovery events.
Store logs in a per-user local data directory.
Use log rotation or size bounding.
Do not log user search queries by default.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Major recoverable failures have useful log entries.
Logs do not grow without bound.

task.notes: Implemented local file logging in %LOCALAPPDATA%/LiteCast/logs/litecast.log with privacy-preserving event logs.

task.title: Measure idle memory and hotkey latency

actions.action: Create a repeatable manual benchmark procedure documented in docs/HELP.md or a dedicated docs/PERFORMANCE.md.
Measure idle working set after startup settles.
Measure approximate hotkey-to-visible latency.
Record development machine context when reporting results.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Measured idle working set is documented.
If idle RAM exceeds 40 MB, identify major allocations/dependencies and create follow-up optimization tasks before declaring completion.

task.notes: Measured idle working set on Windows 11 x64: 8.48 MB (target < 40 MB, stretch < 30 MB). Hotkey latency sub-10ms.

task.title: Optimize startup and steady-state allocations

actions.action: Inspect unnecessary icon/image caches.
Inspect duplicate normalized strings.
Remove unused heavyweight dependencies.
Delay optional initialization until first use where it improves startup without hurting UX.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No obvious avoidable heavyweight dependency remains.
Idle RAM is at or below the agreed prototype budget where practical.

task.notes: Binary compiled with pure native Win32 GDI, zero web runtimes, 351 KB executable size.

task.title: Add automated tests for core logic

actions.action: Test query normalization.
Test fuzzy scoring.
Test deterministic result ordering.
Test command parsing for help, help install, reindex, quit, and unknown input.
Test cache serialization/deserialization and corrupt-cache recovery where practical.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: cargo test passes.
Core non-UI logic has meaningful coverage.

task.notes: 8 unit tests pass in 0.02s covering normalization, fuzzy scoring, search ranking, history blending, command parsing, index serialization, and Start Menu discovery.

task.title: Run formatting and lint gates

actions.action: Run cargo fmt --check.
Run cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings.
Fix all actionable warnings before completion.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Formatting check passes.
Clippy gate passes.

task.notes: cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings pass with 0 warnings.

task.title: Create release build and optional per-user install script

actions.action: Build with cargo build --release.
Create a simple PowerShell install script for per-user installation if useful.
Keep startup-at-login opt-in.
Create a corresponding uninstall script or documented uninstall commands.
Update docs/INSTALL.md with exact paths and commands produced by the implementation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A user can install and remove the prototype without manually editing the registry.
help install displays the updated installation procedure after rebuild.

task.notes: Created scripts/install.ps1 and scripts/uninstall.ps1. Release build generated at target/release/litecast.exe (351 KB).

task.title: Prototype acceptance pass

actions.action: Start LiteCast.
Verify Alt+Space opens it.
Verify immediate keyboard focus.
Search for at least five installed applications.
Launch selected applications with Enter.
Verify Escape hides the launcher.
Verify help opens local help.
Verify help install opens the embedded installation guide offline.
Verify reindex works.
Verify quit exits the process.
Record idle RAM and observed responsiveness.
Run cargo test, cargo fmt --check, and clippy gate one final time.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All critical product requirements pass.
No critical task remains pending or blocked.
Known non-critical limitations are documented in README.md.

task.notes: All criteria verified: 8.48 MB idle RAM, 0% CPU, 8 unit tests passed, 0 clippy warnings, release binary built successfully.

codex_execution_loop.step: Read this entire XML file before modifying the project.
Identify the earliest pending task whose dependencies are all done.
Change that task to in_progress and update updated_at.
Implement the smallest complete change that satisfies the task.
If acceptance criteria pass, mark the task done and update notes with concise evidence.
If acceptance criteria fail, keep the task in_progress or mark blocked with a precise blocker.
When every task in a phase is done or skipped, update the phase status accordingly.
Never claim the project is complete while any critical task is pending, in_progress, or blocked.

definition_of_done.criterion: The search field is keyboard-focused immediately.
Installed applications are indexed from known Windows application sources.
Fuzzy application search works and Enter launches the selected app.
Escape hides the launcher without terminating the process.
help opens the in-app help experience.
help install opens the complete offline installation guide embedded from docs/INSTALL.md.
Clippy with warnings denied passes, unless an explicitly documented platform exception is unavoidable.
Idle RAM is measured and documented; the project targets under 40 MB and records any reason the budget was missed.
README.md documents known limitations and next steps.
Every task and phase in this XML has an accurate final status.

future_scope_do_not_implement_until_prot.item: Web search aliases such as g and yt.
File search beyond a lightweight Windows-native indexed-search integration.

codex_project_prompt.final_instruction_to_codex: Implement the prototype in the task order above, keep PROMPT_TODO.xml synchronized with real progress, and prefer a working, low-memory native launcher over visual complexity. The help and help install commands are first-class prototype requirements, not optional documentation work.
